sources_considered.why: Establishes the date and scope of the MUSE study.
Reports unlearning failures and explicitly distinguishes removal-set scaling from total training-data scaling.
Dated experiments provide a counterweight: some measured social bias can be reduced through unlearning.
Later conference version is relevant, but the explicitly dated preprint is used for the evidence record.
Reports efficient debiasing methods but does not directly test the asserted relationship with total training-data consumption.
Duplicates MUSE; the dated paper version is used.

evidence_items.locator: Section 7, Conclusion; scaling experiment in section 5.2, C5
evidence_items.explanation: MUSE finds practical failures in tested language-model unlearning methods. Its scaling experiment varies the amount to be removed, which does not establish the claimed effect of total training-data consumption on bias removal.

The study reports measurable bias reduction, limiting an interpretation that learned bias cannot be changed. It does not demonstrate complete removal or test whether additional training data makes removal harder.

unresolved_gaps: No reviewed experiment isolates total training-data consumption as the cause of increased bias-removal difficulty.
The cited experiments do not directly evaluate the February 2023 ChatGPT model.
Successful reduction of a bias score is not proof that the underlying learned information has been removed.
